name: ChapterBridge
card_status: Daily use: A small group of readers at home and on the road.
users: Me and a small group of other readers, at home and on the road.
card_line: An app that matches ebooks to audiobooks, highlights each spoken word, and uses one bookmark.
page_subtitle: An app that matches ebooks to audiobooks, highlights each spoken word, and syncs my place.
time_to_build: A few hours of building with Codex and Claude, then a few days of testing and tweaks

snapshot.problem: Ebooks and audiobooks didn't know about each other, so switching from reading to listening meant hunting for my place and in different apps.
snapshot.what_i_built: A Windows app that lines up an ebook with its audiobook, and an Android app that reads, plays, and keeps one place.
snapshot.result: One streamlined app for reading and listening, so I never lose my place or juggle separate apps. I've finished two books, reading at night and listening while driving, and I'm on the third.

problem: I read the ebook at night and listen to the audiobook in the car, and the two copies never knew about each other. Every switch meant scrubbing a 20-plus-hour recording for the scene I'd stopped on, or paging through the ebook to find where the narrator left off. Audio tracks don't line up with chapters, so even a close guess left me hunting. The books are files I already own, so the tool had to work with my copies, on my own computer, without breaking any copy protection.

how_it_works.text: I add an ebook and its audiobook on my PC, either one file or a stack of tracks put in order.
Speech recognition transcribes the narration on my own computer, in 10-minute chunks it can resume after a restart.
Code matches the transcript to the ebook word by word in reading order, and words it can't place stay untimed instead of guessed.
The finished book goes to my private Google Drive, and the phone checks every byte of its download before marking it ready offline.
I read, listen, or use Read Along, which highlights each word as it's spoken, and all three share one saved place.
Each move of my place is saved as a new entry that never replaces an old one, and it syncs between the PC and phone.
If both devices moved while apart, the app shows both places and I pick the one to keep.

decisions.decision: I choose when two places disagree.
decisions.reason: Every saved place is kept, and the database can add places but not change them. When the phone and PC moved separately, the app asks me. It never picks by clock time or by which is farther along.

decisions.decision: Speech recognition listens, and code decides what matches.
decisions.reason: The recognizer turns audio into words with rough times. Code matches them to the ebook in order and leaves the rest untimed, so a gap clears the highlight.

decisions.decision: My books stay on my machines and my Drive.
decisions.reason: The PC services answer only to the PC. Google access covers only files the app made, and only my account can read my places.

decisions.decision: It only handles books I own and can open.
decisions.reason: It reads plain EPUB and common audio. It doesn't buy or unlock books, and an encrypted ebook stops the import.

decisions.decision: Real reading removed prompts I didn't need.
decisions.reason: Early versions stopped at every contents page and cast list the narrator skips. Now the app skips to the next spoken point and flags only a missed story chapter.

results.label: Reading, listening, PC, and phone all pick up from it.
The app finds where each word is spoken in the audio.
Speech recognition runs on my PC. Books stay in my own Drive.
Synced books can be saved to device, so internet dead zones are irrelevant while on the go.

checks.label: Word matching inside chapters. Non-spoken text (forwards, publisher info) stays untimed, not guessed.
Enough memory for a full-book import now. The old code failed a 256 MB test after a phone crash.
Automated tests performed after new builds, before deployment.

next: Sync in the background, so my place is current before I sit at the PC. Today the phone syncs only while the app is open.
Add Android Auto, so I can pick a chapter from the car's screen. Today the car just plays the phone's audio.
